subject.title: fix(gateway-client): unref WS socket in beginStop() to fix CLI hang (#88230)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a guarded dependency on `ws._socket` to release the event-loop handle for one-shot gateway-client shutdown after current-head live proof confirms the protocol-mediated path?
rationale: The code deliberately relies on an upgrade-sensitive private dependency contract; its fallback is safe from exceptions but leaves the original availability failure possible, so product/runtime ownership must decide whether that tradeoff is acceptable.

options.title: Accept with refreshed proof
options.body: Require a redacted current-head real-socket or authenticated CLI transcript for both `stop()` and awaited `stopAndWait()`, then accept the guarded private-contract tradeoff.

options.title: Require a supported lifecycle seam
options.body: Pause this PR and pursue a public gateway or transport shutdown API that releases the handle without reading `ws` internals.

recommendation.title: Accept with refreshed proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted current-head real-socket or authenticated CLI transcript for both `stop()` and awaited `stopAndWait()`, then accept the guarded private-contract tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identified the exact dependency-contract decision and requested upgrade-safety context for it.
